entries.title: Cards in the text open their own panel
entries.body: When you point at an underlined glossary term, a highlighted quote or a cited work in the article, the card that appears ends with a button that opens the matching panel: Open in Glossary, Open in Quotes, or the new Open in Sources. Glossary and Sources scroll straight to that term or work, so you land on the row you were asking about rather than at the top of a list.

entries.title: Out-of-date notices can be closed
entries.body: The notice saying a panel may be out of date for the current article can be closed in most panels, including Glossary, Ideas, Summary, Quotes, Skim, Search and Sources, without making it again. On your own articles it stays closed; progress and Stop stay visible if a panel is being made. The Quiz notice still cannot be closed.

entries.title: Authors' institutions found on more pages
entries.body: When you add an article from the web that lists its authors but not where they work, the AI now reads the opening of the page to find each author's institution, and keeps it only when it can tell which author it belongs to. The privacy page says what the AI is shown for this.

entries.title: Search no longer breaks off on long papers
entries.body: On very long papers, Search could stop partway through its answer and show an error instead of the passages it found. It now has room to finish. The same kind of cut-off could give an added PDF a worse title; that has room to finish too.
